_readme: Boston's signature dishes - edited by hand. A restaurant whose own description says it is known for one of these gets a 'Local specialty' chip and a few points (restaurants/scoring.py).
Fields: key (stable id, used in data/specialties/<city>.json), label (shown on the page), also_called (other names the classifier should accept), why (one line, for people editing this file).

dishes.label: Lobster roll
dishes.why: New England's best-known sandwich; Boston has dozens of dedicated spots.

dishes.label: Lobster
dishes.why: Local catch served whole, steamed or baked - distinct from the roll.

dishes.label: Clam chowder
dishes.why: The cream-based New England chowder is a Boston staple.

dishes.label: Local oysters
dishes.why: Massachusetts oysters (Wellfleet, Duxbury, Island Creek) are a point of local pride.

dishes.label: Fried clams
dishes.why: Whole-belly fried clams are a North Shore invention.

dishes.label: Steamers
dishes.why: Steamed soft-shell clams with broth and butter.

dishes.label: Local cod & haddock
dishes.why: Scrod (young cod or haddock) is the classic Boston fish.

dishes.label: New England scallops
dishes.why: New Bedford lands more scallops than any other US port.

dishes.label: North Shore roast beef
dishes.why: Rare roast beef on an onion roll with sauce, mayo and cheese - a Greater Boston original.

dishes.label: South Shore bar pizza
dishes.why: Thin, crispy-edged pan pizza from the South Shore.

dishes.label: Boston cream pie
dishes.why: Created at the Omni Parker House; the official state dessert.

dishes.label: North End cannoli
dishes.why: The North End's Italian bakeries are a Boston institution.

dishes.label: Boston baked beans
dishes.why: Molasses-baked beans gave Boston the nickname 'Beantown'.

dishes.label: Indian pudding
dishes.why: Colonial-era cornmeal and molasses dessert, still served at old Boston restaurants.
